top4.why: Financials is the only leading sector whose gains are spread across many names: it beat SPY three weeks running with no single stock carrying it. It also gains most directly from the brief's hawkish front-end regime, because live September hike odds improve carry and rate-volatility income; the main risk is that the Sep 4 jobs report, which this brief predates, turns a labor crack into a credit scare.

Healthcare has the best defensive setup in the brief: the breakout retest held, MRK and AMGN made fresh 52-week highs, and large pharma is not very sensitive to interest rates going into a pre-FOMC week with a live hike. The Aug 31 MFN drug-pricing announcement came after this brief's Aug 28 data, so I don't know how it landed, but by the Tuesday open it will already be priced in.

It was the top sector of the week and held up through Warsh's hawkish Friday, helped by META's legal peace and investors sheltering in telecom, so it is a less rate-sensitive way to own growth than semis, which are being sold into strength. It is still below its 200-day average, so I treat it as a recovery trade rather than an established trend.

The week was a rejection at resistance, not a breakdown, and tobacco rallied on Warsh's hawkish Friday, which shows buyers still want defensives even as rates rise. With the VIX complacent, VVIX rising, a live FOMC the following week and weak September seasonality, the rotation needs one low-beta hedge.
